title: Security & Compliance Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk & Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational standards and procedures for RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response for security events, compliance evidence workflows, and the formal risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineering, SRE, security, and compliance stakeholders responsible for design, implementation, and audit readiness.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane services, customer-facing APIs, and components that process or store customer data.
- Includes hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where Redwood controls any part of the control plane or operational tooling.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific contractual controls for Private deployments; those are captured in the customer's deployment runbook.

Guiding Principles
- Least privilege everywhere: roles and service accounts should have the minimum permissions required.
- Audit-first: all security-relevant actions must be logged and retained according to policy.
- Regionally explicit data handling: data locality and retention are explicit for each dataset.
- Practicable evidence: evidence artifacts must be indexed and discoverable for audits.

RBAC & Authentication
Overview
Redwood uses role-based access control for human and machine identities across the console, APIs, and internal tooling. Primary identity sources: SSO (Okta), SCIM provisioning for users/groups, short-lived service credentials for automation.

Roles and Role Lifecycle
- Built-in roles: org-admin, security-admin, infra-engineer, platform-operator, developer, support-agent, read-only-audit.
- Custom roles: permitted but require approver from Security for any role granting write/modify to production resources.
- Role provisioning steps:
  1. Request via internal access request form (see access-and-permissions documentation).
  2. Approver: team manager + security reviewer for production scopes.
  3. SCIM provisioning event recorded in audit logs.
  4. Review TTL/recertification at 90-day cycle for elevated roles.

Authentication Controls
- Primary SSO: Okta with enforced MFA (TOTP + either push or U2F for admins).
- Service accounts: must use short-lived tokens (workload identity or vault-issued) with automatic rotation.
- API keys: allowed only for service-to-service integration; keys must be bound to a single purpose and rotated every 30 days.
- Privileged access: require Just-in-Time (JIT) actuation via access request flow and ephemeral credentials.

Service Account & Secret Management
- Secrets are stored in Vault (customer KMS used in Private where required).
- Secrets access requires policy-based approval; access is logged and audited.
- Emergency access (break-glass) is logged and requires post-hoc review within 48 hours.

Audit Logging
Logging Requirements
- All authentication events, role grants/revocations, SSO/SCIM provisioning, infrastructure changes (deploys, schema migrations), data export requests, and break-glass events must be logged.
- Log format: structured JSON with fields: timestamp, actor, actor_type (user/service), action, resource, resource_id, request_id, outcome, ip, region.
- Traceability: every high-risk change must include a request_id linking code change, PR, and deployment job.

Retention and Aggregation
- Security-critical logs: retained for 3 years in immutable storage for audit purposes.
- Operational logs: retained for 90 days in hot storage, 365 days in warm storage.
- Sensitive access logs (customer data access): retained for 7 years when required by contractual/regulatory obligations.

Log Delivery and Monitoring
- Central logging pipeline: Fluentd -> immutable S3 buckets -> SIEM (Splunk/Datadog).
- Real-time alerting for: failed auth spikes, anomalous privilege escalations, high-volume data egress, and audit log tampering.
- Regular integrity scans: weekly checksum verification of immutable log buckets.

Data Residency & Retention
Data Classification
- PII, Customer Data, Internal Confidential, Public.
- Each dataset has metadata: owner, region, retention policy, encryption-at-rest key (KMS ARN).

Regional Controls
- Hosted customer data is stored in the region selected during account onboarding. Cross-region replication only occurs when explicitly enabled and documented in the customer contract.
- Private deployments follow customer-supplied region controls and on-prem policies.

Retention Policy (summary)
- Authentication events: 3 years (immutable logs).
- API call logs: 1 year (aggregated metrics retained 3 years).
- Customer prompt history (if enabled): 90 days (configurable).
- Backups (control plane config): 1 year (encrypted).
- Audit evidence artifacts: 7 years.

Deletion & Right-to-be-forgotten
- Data deletion requests follow the DSR runbook: validate -> identify stores -> schedule deletion/obfuscation -> update audit evidence.
- Deletion exceptions for legal holds are documented in the legal hold register and reviewed by Legal.

Secure SDLC
Minimum Requirements
- Threat modeling for high-risk services at design review and annually.
- Mandatory code review for production changes; at least one independent reviewer for security-impacting changes.
- Automated CI checks: SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, license checks, unit/integration tests.
- Pre-prod must mirror production auth and logging; use feature flags for rollout.

Release & Deployment Controls
- Canary and progressive rollouts for infra/runtime changes; rollback plan documented in PR.
- Deployment approvals: automatic change record; security sign-off required for changes to auth/audit/data pipelines.

Developer Guidance & Checklists
- PR checklist: security impact, threat model link, test coverage, monitoring hooks, rollback steps, runbook updates.
- Dependency upgrade policy: critical fixes applied within 7 days; regular upgrades on a 30/90 day cadence.

Incident Response (Security) Procedures
Detection & Triage
- Sources: SIEM, monitoring, customer reports, external intel.
- Triage levels: P1 (data exfiltration/system compromise), P2 (privilege escalation attempt), P3 (suspicious activity, non-prod impact).

Incident Playbook (high-level)
1. Detect & Acknowledge: Incident owner acknowledges within 15 minutes.
2. Triage & Classify: determine scope and severity.
3. Contain & Mitigate: apply ACLs, rotate keys, block attacker ingress, isolate nodes.
4. Investigate & Forensics: preserve logs (immutable snapshot), capture memory if applicable, document chain-of-custody.
5. Remediate & Recover: deploy patch/rollback, validate integrity, restore services.
6. Notification & Disclosure: notify internal stakeholders within 1 hour for P1; customer notification per contractual SLAs (initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed exposure).
7. Postmortem & Remediation Plan: publish blameless postmortem within 7 business days for P1, 15 business days for P2.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Incident Commander: Senior Security Engineer.
- Forensics Lead: SRE/Infra engineer.
- Communications: Legal + Customer Success.
- Escalation path: on-call -> security manager -> CTO for P1s.

Evidence Preservation
- Preserve immutable copies of logs and snapshots in separate restricted storage.
- Catalog artifacts with metadata: incident_id, artifact_type, collector, retention_until.

Compliance Evidence Workflows
Control Mapping & Evidence Types
- Controls map to artifacts: config snapshots, access policy documents, audit logs, PRs/CI artifacts, runbook execution logs, attestations.

Evidence Lifecycle
- Creation: automated exports where possible.
- Indexing: Compliance Evidence Index (CEI) with tags: control_id, owner, created_at, retention_until.
- Review cadence: quarterly evidence reviews for SOC2/ISO; ad-hoc for customer audits.

Audit Request Response
1. Triage request and map controls to CEI artifacts.
2. Pull artifacts and validate integrity checksums.
3. Prepare auditor bundle and obtain security/legal approval.
4. Provide read-only access or delivery per NDA.
5. Log request in Audit Request Tracker with timestamps and approvers.

Artifacts & Retention
- Canonical artifacts in immutable storage with access logs and checksums.
- Retention baseline: 7 years unless contractually varied.

Risk & Exceptions Process
Exception Request Flow
1. Submit exception request with justification, scope, duration, compensating controls.
2. Security performs risk assessment and assigns owner.
3. Approval gates: security lead -> CTO -> CRO/Board for high risk.
4. Record exceptions in Risk Register with review date and mitigations.

Compensating Controls Examples
- Temporary least-privilege exception: continuous monitoring, shorter TTL, weekly access review.
- KMS integration unavailable: envelope encryption + additional audit hooks.

Risk Register & Reporting
- Risk Register fields: request_id, description, owner, severity, compensating_controls, approval_chain, expiry_date.
- Quarterly risk review by Security and Product.

Ownership, Contacts & Escalations
- Document owner: Security Documentation Lead (Aisha Patel).
- Operational contacts: Security on-call, SRE Lead (Liam Chen), Platform Eng Manager (Maya Rodriguez).
- Legal & Privacy: Legal Counsel (Evan Morgan).
- Urgent escalations via PagerDuty route "security-critical".

Change History & Review
- Review cadence: annual; ad-hoc for major control changes.
- Change log maintained in CEI update stream.

Appendices
A. Quick operational commands
- Export IAM policy example:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/iam/policies?format=json > iam-policy-$(date +%F).json
- Snapshot audit logs to immutable bucket example:
  aws s3 cp --acl bucket-owner-full-control /var/logs/security/ s3://redwood-audit-immutable/$(date +%F)/ --storage-class GLACIER

B. Templates
- Exception request template: see /confluence/policies-and-process/exception-request-template.
- Incident report template: see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template.

C. References
- SOC2 evidence matrix and CEI mappings (internal).
- Related confluence pages listed in metadata.

For deployment-specific applicability (Dedicated/Private), open a review request with Security including deployment details so the playbook can be augmented for contract-specific controls.
